message.content:
**Los Angeles (Pacific Time) vs. Berlin (Central European Time)**  

| Period | LA Time Zone | Berlin Time Zone | UTC Offset | Difference |
|--------|--------------|------------------|------------|------------|
| **Standard time** (winter, when both are on standard time) | Pacific Standard Time (PST) – UTC‑8 | Central European Time (CET) – UTC+1 | 9 hours (Berlin ahead) |
| **Daylight‑saving overlap** (when one is on DST and the other isn’t) | 1–2 weeks in late March & late October | 1–2 weeks in late March & late October | 8 hours (Berlin ahead) |
| **Both on daylight saving** (summer) | Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) – UTC‑7 | Central European Summer Time (CEST) – UTC+2 | 9 hours (Berlin ahead) |

### Why the difference changes

- **US DST** starts on the second Sunday in March and ends on the first Sunday in November.  
- **European DST** starts on the last Sunday in March and ends on the last Sunday in October.

During the brief overlap windows (late March and late October) one region has switched to DST while the other has not, reducing the time difference to **8 hours**. For the rest of the year, the difference is **9 hours** with Berlin always ahead of Los Angeles.

Then from Oct 29 to Nov 5, LA still on DST but Berlin back to CET: difference 8 hours again. So the difference varies between 8 and 9 hours depending on DST overlap.
